topic: Urgent Matter — Proportionate Emergency / Social / Legal Deadline Triage
user_query: Applicant may face a time-sensitive legal issue, safety concern, basic-needs crisis, or another urgent matter. Classify the urgency without treating generic legal language as a crisis.
variations: Applicant says they are in danger right now.
Applicant has a hearing, filing deadline, reporting date, or immigration deadline within 14 days.
Applicant is about to be evicted or has nowhere safe to stay tonight.
Applicant says they have no food or money for their family.
Applicant is in police custody, detention, or faces imminent removal.
Applicant mentions court, police, being charged, bail, sentencing, or jail, but gives no facts showing immediate safety, basic-needs, detention, or deadline risk.
part_a_general_info: This entry is a risk-classification gate. Do not equate legal seriousness with emergency risk. Words like court, charged, sentenced, police, lawyer, bail, jail, hearing, or custody are not enough by themselves to ask crisis questions. Escalate only where the facts show one of these categories: (1) immediate safety or crisis: current violence, credible threats, self-harm/suicide risk, medical emergency, unlawful coercion, or someone is unsafe right now; (2) basic needs or child welfare: no safe place tonight, imminent homelessness, no food or money for basic needs, urgent child welfare risk; (3) legal/procedural deadline: court date, filing deadline, appeal deadline, reporting/surrender date, immigration pass/removal deadline, injunction/PPO hearing, or police/custody step within 14 days; (4) unclear or too complex: multiple urgent signals, contradictory facts, or the intern cannot safely classify the matter. For legal/procedural urgency, ask legally useful deadline and representation questions, not alarmist safety questions unless safety facts are present. For safety or self-harm, emergency/social support runs before legal triage. For basic needs, SSO/FSC support runs concurrently with legal triage. Each path must end in a route or resume the parent workflow; do not loop.
triage_questions: Q1: Which urgent concern is actually present: immediate safety or crisis; basic needs or child welfare; legal/procedural deadline; no urgent issue beyond legal seriousness; or unclear/too complex?
Q2: Is there an immediate threat to the applicant's (or someone else's) life, physical safety, or risk of self-harm right now?
Q3: Is the urgent issue about basic needs or child welfare, such as no safe place tonight, imminent homelessness, no food, no money, or a child at immediate risk?

Q4: Is there a specific legal or procedural deadline within 14 days that requires action, such as a court/hearing date, filing deadline, reporting/surrender date, immigration deadline, injunction/PPO hearing, or police/custody step?
Q5: After the urgent support or deadline pathway is identified, is there still a legal matter that needs normal PBSG triage?

Q3.if_not_sure: Route F (Human Review — social support risk unclear)

routing: Route A (Emergency / Crisis Support — IMMEDIATE): Use only for facts showing immediate safety, physical danger, medical emergency, or self-harm/suicide risk. Say to the applicant: "The most important thing right now is your immediate safety. Please call 999 for police or 995 for ambulance now. If this is about violence or harassment, you may also contact NAVH at 1800-777-0000. If this is about self-harm or suicide, you may contact National Mindline at 1771." Do not continue legal triage while immediate safety is at risk. After the emergency step, note the concern and escalate to PBSG Staff.

Route B (SSO / FSC / Child Welfare Support — PRIMARY): Use for imminent homelessness, no safe place tonight, no food or money for basic needs, or urgent child welfare/social support needs. Say: "This sounds like an immediate support need. Let me help you identify the nearest Social Service Office or Family Service Centre, and we can still note the legal issue if there is one." Look up SSO/FSC using the applicant's postal code. If legal triage remains, continue concurrently to Route D or the parent workflow.

Route C (Urgent Legal Consultation Assessment): Use for a concrete legal or procedural deadline within 14 days, without assuming the applicant is in physical danger. Say: "Because there is a near deadline, I will take down the key details and ask PBSG Staff to assess whether urgent legal consultation is available. I cannot promise a same-day appointment, but I will flag the timing clearly." Take down the deadline date, type of deadline, current representation status, relevant court/police/immigration documents if any, and the underlying legal topic. Resume GEN3-T01 or the parent workflow after recording the urgent legal pathway.

Route D (Return to GEN3-T01): Use when there is no immediate safety/basic-needs crisis, or after the urgent pathway has been identified and a legal matter still needs triage. Return to the active parent workflow if GEN3-T06 was nested under GEN3-T02 or GEN3-T03; otherwise return to GEN3-T01.

Route E (Document Urgent Intake and Close): Use when the urgent support information has been provided and no legal matter remains for PBSG triage. Record the concern, pathway shared, and any referral information. Inform applicant that they may call PBSG again if a legal matter emerges later.

Route F (Human Review — Urgency or Vulnerability Too Complex): Use when the facts contain multiple urgent signals, contradictory information, unclear safety risk, uncertain deadline impact, possible coercion, or anything the intern cannot confidently classify. Take down the applicant's contact details, the exact facts creating concern, any date/deadline, and any immediate support already shared. Escalate to PBSG Staff the same day. Do not keep asking follow-up questions in a loop.

Route F.script: I need PBSG Staff to assess this because the urgent or vulnerability factors are not clear enough for me to classify safely. I will record the key facts and ask PBSG Staff to follow up.

Escalate to PBSG Staff the same day.
Do not attempt to advise on the legal merits.
caveats: This route prevents looping when urgency, vulnerability, and multiple legal topics overlap.

GEN3-T01: Escalate to GEN3-T06 when first-contact facts show immediate danger, no safe place tonight, no food/basic needs, detention, immigration removal, or a concrete deadline within 14 days.
Do not escalate merely because the applicant says they need help, has a legal problem, or sounds worried.
GEN3-T02: Escalate to GEN3-T06 Route C when the criminal matter has a court/hearing/reporting/appeal deadline within 14 days, or the applicant is currently detained or in police custody.

Do not escalate to safety questions merely because the applicant says charged, police, bail, lawyer, sentenced, jail, or court unless there is an immediate safety, custody, deprivation, or deadline fact.
GEN3-T03: Escalate to GEN3-T06 Route A where there is current family violence, threats, stalking, coercive control, unsafe housing, self-harm, or immediate risk to a child.
Escalate to GEN3-T06 Route C where there is a PPO/injunction/custody/maintenance/divorce deadline within 14 days without safety facts.
Do not treat every family court mention as an emergency.
GEN3-T04: Escalate to GEN3-T06 Route B for imminent eviction/homelessness, no basic needs, or urgent social support needs.
Escalate to GEN3-T06 Route C for filing deadlines, appeal deadlines, injunction hearings, or other civil deadlines within 14 days.
Do not escalate merely because the issue is stressful, expensive, or legally serious.
GEN3-T13: Escalate to GEN3-T06 only when vulnerability facts also show immediate safety, basic-needs, child welfare, mental-health crisis, detention, immigration, or deadline risk.
Do not escalate to urgency solely because the applicant is elderly, speaks limited English, has a disability, or has a social worker unless there is a time-sensitive or safety consequence.

guardrail: • Under s 33 of the Legal Profession Act 1966, only qualified, practising lawyers may give legal advice. You must NEVER: (a) interpret a legal document for the applicant; (b) apply the law to the applicant's facts; (c) predict the outcome of a case; (d) tell the applicant what they should do legally. • You MAY: (a) confirm scheme eligibility against objective criteria; (b) read out scheme descriptions verbatim; (c) explain PBSG hotline operations; (d) take down particulars and escalate to PBSG Staff. • If the applicant insists on legal advice, respond: “I’m an intern/volunteer and I’m not able to give legal advice. What I can do is help you find the right legal help avenue or direct you to a qualified lawyer.” • If in doubt at any point — escalate to PBSG Staff. • Protect applicant confidentiality. Do not discuss the applicant outside the hotline context. Do not retain personal data on personal devices and/or beyond the PBSG volunteering period.
